calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number
calibration.basis: Estimated from the supplied description; the example was not opened or independently tested.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and offer Hide times.
primary_action.observed: The focused button changed to Hide times; Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25.

A-1440.edge_observation: Enter again hid both times, retained both names and statuses, and returned the focused button to Show times. The Bay B callout remained prominent.
A-1440.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and neither time was visible. The displayed times matched the task.
A-1440.strength: The large Bay B callout and clear filled toggle make both the exception and action easy to find.
A-1440.weakness: The delayed row itself has less color emphasis than the on-time row, and the filled toggle competes with the exception accent.
A-1440.repair: Give the delayed row the exception accent while keeping the toggle visibly actionable.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and offer Hide times.
primary_action.observed: The focused button changed to Hide times; 09:10 and 09:25 appeared beside the corresponding rows.

A-390.edge_observation: Enter again hid both times while preserving names, statuses, focus, and the Bay B callout.
A-390.fact_check: The initial view showed Bay A On time and Bay B Delayed with both times hidden; both expected times appeared after activation.
A-390.strength: The stacked layout keeps the toggle, exception, and both rows visible and legible at 390 CSS pixels.
A-390.weakness: The on-time status has more color emphasis than the delayed status in the list.
A-390.repair: Apply the exception accent to the delayed status and retain the explicit status text.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and offer Hide times.
primary_action.observed: The focused button changed to Hide times; Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25.

B-1440.edge_observation: Enter again hid both times, retained both names and statuses, and returned focus to Show times. The exception remained the dominant visual element.
B-1440.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and neither time was visible. The displayed times matched the task.
B-1440.strength: The broad peach Bay B panel and matching delayed status create a strong, consistent path to the exception.
B-1440.weakness: The dark outlined Show times button is less prominent against the background than A's filled control.
B-1440.repair: Strengthen the button boundary or fill while preserving the exception panel as the visual focal point.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and offer Hide times.
primary_action.observed: The focused button changed to Hide times; 09:10 and 09:25 appeared beside the corresponding rows.

B-390.edge_observation: Enter again hid both times while preserving names, statuses, focus, and the prominent Bay B panel.
B-390.fact_check: The initial view showed Bay A On time and Bay B Delayed with both times hidden; both expected times appeared after activation.
B-390.strength: The exception remains immediately identifiable in both the panel and the list, with no visible clipping.
B-390.weakness: The outlined action is visually quiet above the much stronger exception panel.
B-390.repair: Increase the action's visual boundary while retaining its clear Show times and Hide times labels.

preference.reason: Both completed the keyboard task at both widths. B more consistently directs attention to the delayed bay through the prominent panel and matching list status; its quieter toggle remains labeled and keyboard accessible, though its boundary could be stronger.

unsupported_claims: The reviews establish the displayed statuses and times, not whether they match an external operational source.
The calibration scores for the withheld example are estimates based only on its description.

superseded_run.reason: The first run passed the action and selected the candidate, but its verifier expected a shared builder session. Repeated with the independent-builder comparison mode.
